exercises.title: Partition, then recurse
exercises.task: Read QuickSort and partition: the pivot ends at its final place, smaller values before it, larger after. Run counts comparisons on random input and on input that is already sorted, with the last element as pivot and then with a random pivot.

exercises.title: Write partition
exercises.task: Fill partition (Lomuto's scheme, the one in e1): the pivot is the last element; walk the range, swapping each smaller value into the front part; finally put the pivot just after that front part and return its index.
hints: i marks the end of the "smaller than the pivot" part: it starts at lo.
For each j from lo to hi-1: if a[j] < pivot, swap a[i] and a[j], then i++.
At the end swap a[i] and a[hi] (the pivot) and return i.

exercises.title: A percentile without sorting
exercises.task: To get a median or a percentile you need the k-th smallest value, not a sorted list. Quickselect (Hoare, 1961): partition, then continue in the one side that holds position k. Write Select; it must compare only through less, which the check counts: about O(n), far fewer than a full sort.
hints: Partition as in e2, but compare with less(a[j], pivot). If the pivot lands at k, done; if k is before it, continue left; otherwise right. A loop, not two recursive calls.
Pick a random pivot (swap a random element of the range to the end first, with rand.Intn): with the last element, sorted input costs n²/2 comparisons, and the check tries sorted input.
Work on a copy (slices.Clone): Select must not reorder the caller's slice.
